$comment: Authored lists. Every list carries a `note` — the curator's sentence or two — because the note is the product. Vinyl Sundays has a full explicit tracklist because it is fully drawn in the file; the rest carry counts that match the Library screen, and build.mjs fills their tracklists from the catalogue. `system: true` marks Liked Songs, the one auto-generated list the brand allows.

playlists.title: Vinyl Sundays
playlists.description: Warm, nostalgic, lo-fi, analog warmth, lazy weekend mornings. Special for sundays and winter.
playlists.note: I've been building this one since we launched. It is the closest thing Kraft has to a house style: tape hiss, room mics, and nothing that sounds finished.

playlists.title: Late Night Heat
playlists.description: Slow, humid, after two in the morning. For rooms with one lamp on.
playlists.note: Made for the drive home after the drive home. Nothing here asks for your full attention until the third song, and then it takes it.

playlists.title: Golden Hour
playlists.description: The forty minutes before the light goes. Nothing urgent, nothing sad.
playlists.note: Records that sound like the last hour of light. I sequence this one backwards, brightest last.

playlists.title: Wildflower Days
playlists.description: Open windows, long grass, and a tape deck that only plays one side.
playlists.note: Folk that isn't precious about it. Half of these were recorded outdoors and you can hear a dog somewhere.

playlists.title: Cassette Dreams
playlists.description: Everything here sounds like it was dubbed twice. That is the point.
playlists.note: Shoegaze and dream pop that still hisses. I kept the ones where the tape is part of the song, not a filter on top of it.

playlists.title: Poolside
playlists.description: Bossa, dub and disco edits for standing in shade you did not plan for.
playlists.note: Cumbia, bossa, and things that move at the speed of a Sunday. Play it loud enough that the neighbours ask.

playlists.title: Garden Sessions
playlists.description: Twenty-five pieces recorded outdoors or pretending to have been.
playlists.note: Ambient for daylight. No drone longer than the kettle takes; this is a list to do something else to.

playlists.title: String Theory
playlists.description: Bowed, plucked, prepared and bowed again. Strings doing unusual work.
playlists.note: Modern composition for strings, mostly. Two of these were recorded in the same church, eleven years apart. You can hear the roof.

playlists.title: Jazz Nights
playlists.description: Small rooms, late sets, and the bar still open. Sequenced as one long night.
playlists.note: Small rooms, late sets, the count-in left in. If you can hear the bassist breathe, it made the cut.

playlists.title: Tropicália
playlists.description: The Brazilian late sixties and everything downstream of it.
playlists.note: The Rio pressings and the Bogotá ones side by side. You can tell them apart by the hiss, and now so can you.

playlists.title: Midnight Sax
playlists.description: One instrument, one hour, no apologies.
playlists.note: Ballads only. I put this together for a friend who couldn't sleep and it has outlived the insomnia.

playlists.title: The Archive
playlists.description: Reissues, restorations and records that nearly did not survive.
playlists.note: Forty tracks of Accra and Lagos crate finds. The liner notes are longer than some of the songs, on purpose.
